prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Houston, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1047; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give you the facts, but I suppose that's fine. I'm the driver of the vehicle involved in the collision.

Q: Understood. Can you describe where you were and what you were doing when the collision occurred?
A: I was in Houston, Texas, heading through an intersection and turning left onto a side street. I had my turn signal on and I was going slowly because the light had just turned yellow.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not clearly. I glanced at oncoming traffic, saw headlights, and started my turn. The next thing I knew, the other car was coming through the intersection and hit the front passenger side of my car.

Q: Were you able to stop or swerve before the impact?
A: No, there wasn't time. It happened in a second or two.

Q: Did you hit your head or lose consciousness?
A: No. I was dazed for a moment but I stayed conscious. I did hit my left arm on the door frame and the steering wheel.

Q: What injuries have you had since the collision?
A: My left wrist was fractured. I was taken to the hospital and they put it in a cast. I've had follow-up appointments and I'm still wearing a splint most of the day.

Q: Have you seen a physician or specialist for the wrist?
A: Yes, an orthopedic doctor. He said I'll need physical therapy for several weeks.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the collision?
A: Only that I was following the rules and I'm trying to get back to normal. My car is still at the repair shop.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Okay, thanks.
